subject: Java
questions: What does the Java compiler (javac) produce from a .java file?
Machine code for the current CPU
javac compiles source code to platform-independent bytecode stored in .class files; the JVM runs that bytecode.
The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) loads and executes bytecode.
Which method signature is the entry point of a standalone Java program?
The JVM looks for public static void main(String[] args).
What does the JIT compiler in the JVM do?
Compiles frequently run bytecode to native code at run time
Just-In-Time compilation turns hot bytecode into native machine code for speed.
Which of these is part of the JDK but not needed just to run a program?
The JDK adds development tools such as javac on top of what is needed to run programs.
What is the main job of the garbage collector?
Free memory used by objects that are no longer reachable
The GC reclaims heap memory of objects that no live reference can reach.
Where are objects created with new stored?
Objects live on the heap; local variables holding references live on the stack.
Which statement about 'Write once, run anywhere' is correct?
Java source must be recompiled for every OS
The same bytecode runs on any platform with a compatible JVM
Java programs run without any runtime
Bytecode is platform independent; each platform supplies its own JVM.
Which keyword imports a class from another package?
Java uses import, e.g. import java.util.List;
What is the default package of classes such as String and Math?
java.lang is imported automatically and contains String, Math, Object, etc.
How many bits does an int use in Java?
int is always 32 bits in Java, regardless of platform.
What is the default value of a boolean field in a class?
Uninitialised boolean fields default to false (local variables have no default).
What is the result of 7 / 2 in Java when both are int?
Integer division truncates toward zero, giving 3.
Which type should you use for a single character such as 'A'?
char holds one 16-bit UTF-16 code unit, written with single quotes.
Which conversion needs an explicit cast?
Narrowing conversions such as double to int may lose data, so they need a cast.
If int x = 5, what is the value of x++ + ++x?
x++ yields 5 (x becomes 6), then ++x makes x 7 and yields 7: 5 + 7 = 12.
Which operator compares two object references for identity?
== on references checks whether they point to the same object; equals() compares content.
What does the && operator do when its left side is false?
&& short-circuits: if the left operand is false the result is false without evaluating the right.
What is the range of a byte in Java?
byte is a signed 8-bit type: -128 to 127.
Which loop always runs its body at least once?
do-while checks its condition after the body.
What does break do inside a loop?
break leaves the innermost loop (or switch).
What does continue do inside a loop?
Skips the rest of this iteration and goes to the next
continue jumps to the next iteration.
In a classic switch statement, what happens without break after a case?
Execution falls through to the next case
Without break, control falls through into the following case labels.
How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 5; i += 2) run its body?
i takes the values 0, 2, 4: three iterations.
Which types can a switch statement use (Java 7+)?
int, char, String, enums and their wrappers
switch works on int-like types, their wrappers, enums and Strings (not long, float or double).
What is the output of: int i = 0; while (i < 3) i++; System.out.println(i);
The loop stops when i reaches 3, which is printed.
What does the ternary expression (a > b) ? a : b return?
The smaller of a and b
The larger of a and b
If a > b it returns a, otherwise b: the maximum.
Which statement leaves a method and optionally gives back a value?
return ends the method, with a value for non-void methods.
What does a labelled break such as break outer; do?
Exits the loop marked with the label outer
Jumps to the label and restarts
A labelled break exits the enclosing statement with that label, e.g. an outer loop.
Why are Java String objects called immutable?
Their content cannot change after creation
They cannot be passed to methods
Methods like toUpperCase return a new String; the original never changes.
Which method compares two strings' contents ignoring case?
equalsIgnoreCase compares characters without regard to case.
substring(begin, end) includes begin and excludes end: indexes 1 and 2.
Which class is best for building a string in a loop with many appends?
StringBuilder is mutable, avoiding a new String object on every append.
It is a field, not a method
length() returns the number of characters: 4.
Evaluation is left to right: "5" + 3 is "53", then + 2 gives "532".
3 + 2 is computed first as int 5, then concatenated with "5": "55".
Which method returns the character at a position?
charAt(index) returns the char at that index.
Where are string literals such as "abc" stored for reuse?
Literals are interned in the string pool so equal literals share one object.
What is the index of the first element of a Java array?
How do you get the number of elements in an array arr?
length is a field of arrays, not a method.
What happens when you access arr[5] in an array of length 5?
Valid indexes are 0-4; index 5 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
What are the elements of new int[3] initialised to?
What are the elements of new String[2] initialised to?
Reference-type array elements default to null.
Which call sorts an int array arr in ascending order?
Can the size of an array change after it is created?
No, arrays have a fixed length
Arrays are fixed-size; use ArrayList for a growable list.
How is a 2D array of 3 rows and 4 columns declared?
Java uses arrays of arrays: new int[3][4].
What does arr.clone() give for an int array?
A new array with the same values
clone on an array makes a shallow copy: a new array with the same elements.
A special method that initialises a new object
A constructor has the class's name, no return type, and runs when an object is created.
What does the keyword this refer to?
this is a reference to the object on which the method or constructor runs.
What does static mean for a field?
It belongs to the class, shared by all objects
A static field has one copy per class, not one per object.
Which access modifier makes a member visible only inside its own class?
private members can only be used within the declaring class.
Using many classes in one file
Hiding fields and exposing behaviour through methods
Encapsulation keeps data private and controls access via methods such as getters and setters.
If a class defines no constructor, what does Java provide?
The compiler adds a default no-arg constructor only when none is declared.
What does a final field mean?
It can be assigned only once
A final variable cannot be reassigned after initialisation.
Can a static method use instance fields directly?
No, it has no this object
Only if the class is final
Static methods run without an instance, so instance fields need an object reference.
Same method name, different parameter lists in one class
Redefining a parent method in a subclass
Calling a method too many times
Overloading is resolved at compile time from the parameter types.
Value (for objects, the value of the reference)
Java is always pass-by-value; for objects the reference is copied.
Which keyword makes a class inherit from another class?
How many classes can a Java class directly extend?
Java has single inheritance for classes (multiple interfaces are allowed).
Two methods with the same name in one class
A subclass providing its own version of an inherited method
Overriding keeps the signature and replaces the behaviour; it is chosen at run time.
What does super() in a constructor do?
super(...) must be the first statement and runs the superclass constructor.
Which class is the root of every Java class hierarchy?
Every class extends java.lang.Object directly or indirectly.
Animal a = new Dog(); a.speak(); Which speak() runs if Dog overrides it?
Dynamic dispatch picks the method of the object's actual class at run time.
Can a final method be overridden?
Asks the compiler to check that the method really overrides one
It is required for every method
If no parent method matches, the compiler reports an error.
Which operator checks if an object is an instance of a class?
obj instanceof Dog is true if obj is a Dog or subclass.
When overriding, can a subclass make a method less accessible (public to private)?
An override may not reduce visibility.
Can you create an object of an abstract class with new?
Only if it has a constructor
Abstract classes cannot be instantiated; only concrete subclasses can.
Which keyword does a class use to implement an interface?
How many interfaces can a class implement?
A class may implement multiple interfaces.
Since Java 8, what can interfaces contain besides abstract methods?
Interfaces can have default and static methods (and private methods since Java 9).
Fields declared in an interface are implicitly ...
Interface fields are constants: public, static and final.
An interface with exactly one abstract method
An abstract class with one method
Functional interfaces such as Runnable can be implemented with lambdas.
Which is true about abstract classes?
They can have both abstract and concrete methods
All their methods must be abstract
Abstract classes can mix abstract methods, implemented methods, fields and constructors.
A concrete class extends an abstract class. What must it do?
Otherwise the class must itself be declared abstract.
Which of these is a functional interface in java.util.function?
Predicate<T> has one abstract method: boolean test(T t).
Which lambda matches Comparator<String> comparing by length?
Comparator.compare takes two arguments and returns an int.
Which block always runs, whether or not an exception occurs?
finally runs after try/catch (except in cases like System.exit).
Checked exceptions such as IOException must be caught or declared with throws.
What happens when you divide an int by zero?
Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException (floating point gives Infinity).
Which keyword declares that a method may throw a checked exception?
Which keyword actually raises an exception?
Calling a method on a null reference throws ...
Runs code in a new thread
Resources declared in try(...) are closed at the end, even after exceptions.
Which class is the superclass of all exceptions and errors?
Throwable has two subclasses: Exception and Error.
RuntimeException and its subclasses (and Errors) are unchecked.
With several catch blocks, which order is correct?
A general catch first would make later specific ones unreachable, which is a compile error.
Which collection keeps insertion order and allows duplicates?
Lists keep order and allow duplicates.
Which collection does not allow duplicate elements?
Sets store each element at most once.
Which Map keeps its keys sorted?
TreeMap is a red-black tree ordered by key.
What does map.get(key) return when the key is missing in a HashMap?
get returns null for absent keys (getOrDefault lets you choose a default).
Average time to look up a key in a HashMap?
Hashing gives constant average lookup time.
Which is faster for frequent insertions in the middle of a list (given an iterator position)?
LinkedList inserts at a known node in O(1); ArrayList shifts elements.
Generics need reference types, so use List<Integer>
Type arguments must be objects; autoboxing converts int to Integer.
Which interface lets you loop with for-each over a collection?
Any Iterable works with the enhanced for loop.
Modifying an ArrayList while looping over it with for-each usually throws ...
The iterator detects structural changes; use iterator.remove() or removeIf.
Which method sorts a List<String> list in natural order?
Collections.sort(list) or list.sort(null) sorts in natural order.
